metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude write a new video-calling engine, or does it wire Zoom's own Meeting SDK into an app you already have? Lands the carry-out that build-zoom-meeting-app assembles a join flow, an embed, or the meeting lifecycle from Zoom's own SDK — it never invents the video engine itself.

beats.narration_text: For this skill, there are exactly four situations it covers: implementing a Meeting SDK join, embedding a meeting in a web or mobile app, handling the lifecycle around a meeting — starting, waiting, ending — or deciding between the Meeting SDK and the Video SDK. Each stays inside Zoom's own developer tools. Ask for something outside those four and there's no mode that covers it.

A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: build-zoom-meeting-app doesn't hand Claude a video-calling engine to invent — it hands Claude Zoom's own Meeting SDK, wired into an app you already have as a join flow, an embed, or the lifecycle around the call.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Ask Claude: I want to add a 'Join Meeting' button to my web app using Zoom's Meeting SDK. Walk me through the pieces I'd need — the SDK, the meeting lifecycle events, and when I'd reach for the Video SDK instead — before writing any code. Liam, in for Bear.
